Thanks for the quick intake. CloudBridge is ready to kick off the GCP Marketplace listing process — they asked that we align procurement and co-sell readiness in the same sprint to avoid duplicate handoffs. Can you share your typical onboarding sprint cadence, and who at Redwood owns the procurement liaison?

- Confirm procurement contact and contract workflow for GCP Marketplace entitlements
- Validate billing codes / SKUs for reserved instances and metered billing
- Outline a 4-week onboarding sprint with milestones (security review, listing assets, pricing, QA)

I attached the standard GCP onboarding template to this email. Proposed time to discuss: Wed 10–11am PT.

Best,

Thanks — and great to meet you all.

Short answers up front: procurement liaison: Lauren Bishop (cc'd). Sprint cadence: we typically do a 3-week rapid sprint + 1 week buffer for procurement/contracting, so aligns with your 4-week ask. I'll attach our internal onboarding checklist and a draft sprint roadmap for CloudBridge so we can iterate before Wed.

Draft sprint (high level):
Week 0 (prework): NDA completed, accounts provisioned, and initial asset drop
Week 1: Security/compliance review (SOC2 docs, data flow diagrams) + billing SKU mapping
Week 2: Listing assets (marketing collateral, screenshots, trial config) + integration tests
Week 3: Listing QA + pricing confirmation + co-sell enablement pack
Week 4: Procurement sign-off & marketplace publish window

Action items for Wed meeting:
- Lauren: confirm procurement intake steps and legal review SLA
- Jonas: confirm technical checklist and required GCP SKU tagging
- Marta / CloudBridge: provide target pricing tiers and trial entitlement logic

Attachments: gcp_onboarding_checklist.xlsx, redwood-gcp-listing-sprint.odt

I'll hold Wed 10–11am PT. If that works, send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Adding procurement details here.

Quick notes:
- Procurement intake: we use a Purchase Order (PO) flow for committed Dedicated contracts and a metered billing flow for hosted usage. For Marketplace listings the common path is: Marketplace terms -> Redwood Master Services Agreement (MSA) -> SOW/Order form for committed capacity.
- Legal review SLA: 5 business days for standard Marketplace terms; expedited 48–72 hours needs CRO approval.
- Required artifacts for procurement handoff: signed MSA (docuSign link), expected usage forecast (monthly RU/month or cN), and billing contact + tax form.

I'll be the point for coordinating the MSA and working with CloudBridge's procurement. For internal routing, please copy procurement@redwood.example.com on any contract docs.

Attachments: procurement-contact-roles.docx

Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Operations

Thanks — a couple technical clarifications from the runtime/ops side:

1) SKU / metering mapping: we need to agree on granularity (instance-hours vs token-units). CloudBridge -- do you expect flat instance pricing for Dedicated or per-token for hosted? That changes the Marketplace SKU design.
2) Security artifacts: please share SOC2 scope and data residency requirements. If CloudBridge expects EU controls, we'll need to surface that earlier.
3) Canary plan: recommend a canary publish to one region then scale; will require a short rollback policy and a fallback model variant for the first 48 hours.

I've attached our canonical runtime checklist so it can be cross-referenced. I'll review expected quotas and submit a GCP billing SKU proposal by EOD Tue.

-Jonas Weber
Senior Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

- CloudBridge prefers metered per-token billing for hosted (primary) and a dedicated tier with reservation SKUs for enterprise customers.
- SOC2 reports available; scope includes our EU region. We will share our evidence bundle ahead of the meeting.
- We'll drop a pricing matrix into the Drive folder and invite procurement@cloudbridge.io to the meeting.

On the procurement side, our team expects to provide a PO for committed Dedicated deals. We will need Redwood's tax and remittance details in the SOW.

See you Wed.
